answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive: every new agent must post a bond that is burned if it colludes, so spawning a thousand ghost accounts costs real value and risks it all. Think of the chain as a wharf where reputations berth — a fresh hull arrives with nothing, while proven vessels earn cargo priority. A gale of fake peers may rock the harbor, but bonded identities weather it because fraud forfeits the deposit, and honest collective stakes grow like opal under pressure: rare, hard, and increasingly brilliant.
